headline: High data-leakage and capability-conflict risk: Airbyte’s broad egress can move business data into ComfyUI’s model/workflow surfaces, while ComfyUI’s offline defaults reduce but do not eliminate pairwise misuse.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airbyte has broad network egress and can call APIs, while ComfyUI exposes files/workflows and runs an asynchronous queue. There is no documented shared channel or direct instruction-parsing bridge, so prompt injection is not default-dangerous. The main pathway would require an unusual manual handoff of Airbyte output into ComfyUI inputs.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies Airbyte-generated text into a ComfyUI prompt or workflow file, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between the agents, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not paste Airbyte output into ComfyUI prompts without review.
Use a strict prompt/template wrapper for any handoff.
Disable any shared queue or folder between the tools.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on all inter-agent handoffs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad egress; ComfyUI touches images, workflows, seeds, and model artifacts and can call its vendor API. Even without a shared filesystem, a manual or orchestrated transfer of Airbyte outputs into ComfyUI can expose business data to image-generation workflows. The pairwise pathway is plausible in default use, but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Airbyte outputs business data into files or prompts consumed by ComfyUI, leakage is possible.
IF ComfyUI is configured to send workflow contents to its vendor API, transferred data may leave the local environment.
mitigations: Avoid passing business data into ComfyUI workflows.
Redact sensitive fields before any handoff.
Use a local-only ComfyUI deployment.
Review outbound destinations for both tools.
requires-engineering: enforce data-class filters at the integration boundary.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airbyte can call APIs and ComfyUI can manage files for models and workflows, but ComfyUI explicitly cannot write the filesystem or modify git state, and supports only one instance. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely. The remaining conflict surface is limited to API-level contention or manual coordination mistakes.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same external API resource, contention may occur.
IF an operator manually synchronizes shared artifacts, race conditions become possible.
mitigations: Assign separate API credentials or endpoints.
Keep ComfyUI read-only for shared artifacts.
Schedule non-overlapping runs.
Use a single orchestrator to serialize access.
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared mutable resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airbyte can produce transformed business data that ComfyUI may consume as workflow inputs or assets, but ComfyUI has no built-in verification of upstream semantics. If Airbyte emits malformed or misleading content, ComfyUI can propagate it into generated outputs or downstream artifacts. The interaction is inferred from documented surfaces, not directly observed.
conditions: IF ComfyUI treats Airbyte output as authoritative input, errors can cascade.
IF Airbyte produces incorrect records that are rendered or embedded by ComfyUI, downstream artifacts may be wrong.
mitigations: Insert a validation step between agents.
Require schema checks on Airbyte outputs.
Have a human review high-impact outputs before generation.
Keep ComfyUI outputs non-authoritative until checked.
requires-engineering: add automated consistency tests at the boundary.

E_compliance.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad egress, while ComfyUI handles model artifacts and can call a vendor API. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, so compliance risk is not provably high; however, any regulated business data routed from Airbyte into ComfyUI could create retention or transfer issues. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise.
conditions: IF regulated business data is routed from Airbyte into ComfyUI, retention and transfer controls must be checked.
IF ComfyUI sends workflow contents to a vendor API, local retention assumptions may be violated.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of ComfyUI inputs.
Document retention for both tools.
Confirm vendor API handling for ComfyUI.
Use separate storage for regulated datasets.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing by data class.
